Reduction techniques transform survival tasks into regression or classification problems.
The main reduction techniques are PEM, DT, PV, IPCW, and CRM.
PEM uses Poisson regression with time at risk as an offset.
DT methods use binary classification on interval indices.
Reduction techniques can handle competing risks and multi-state settings.
Time-varying effects are modeled as interaction terms with time.
The transformed data can be analyzed with standard ML/DL tools.
Reduction techniques do not require custom survival-specific learners.
They can predict hazards, survival probabilities, and cumulative incidence functions.
The offset in PEM is the logarithm of the time at risk.
Left-truncation and time-varying features are handled by data transformation.
Benchmark results show competitive performance with specialized survival learners.
The unified framework enables systematic comparison of reduction techniques.
Competing risks are handled by creating separate datasets for each event type.
Counterfactual transitions are used for competing risks and multi-state models.
The paper provides a principled implementation for standard ML workflows.
Reduction techniques can model non-proportional hazards.
The transformation parameters are reused for test data prediction.
The paper illustrates each reduction with dedicated examples.
Quantitative benchmark comparisons are performed against established methods.
The framework is applicable to many survival tasks, including recurrent events.
Reduction techniques do not make strong assumptions about the underlying distribution.
They can use any off-the-shelf ML/DL implementation for regression or classification.
The paper discusses software implementations for reduction techniques.
The contributions include a unified framework, overview of strengths and weaknesses, and benchmark analysis.
